chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The ritual bath (Ghusl) on Friday is obligatory for men and women in the city (not traveling), and for men during travel, and it is not obligatory for women during travel.
And in another report, it was permitted for women during travel due to the scarcity of water.
ai.seo_question: Is the Friday bath obligatory for women when traveling?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the obligatory nature of Ghusl al-Jumu'ah, distinguishing between residents and travelers while highlighting a specific concession for women during travel due to water scarcity. It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on balancing ritual purity with practical ease (rukhas), particularly in the context of the four major hadith collections. The ruling underscores the communal significance of Friday as a day of gathering and spiritual renewal for both genders.
